summary: Version 1 passes 1 of its 4 checks, so it does not pass its own test yet. Known Mars analogs beat ordinary places: 56% of pairs (pass mark 80%). Known Mars analogs beat plain deserts: 33% of pairs (pass mark 60%). Polar and highland analogs beat ordinary places: 45% of pairs (pass mark 80%). Basalt and crater sites beat ordinary places on terrain: 84% of pairs (pass mark 80%). Most misses are small, rugged or icy analogs that fill only part of a 50 km cell, or polar sites whose cold matches but whose small day-to-night swing, low sun and clear air do not match Jezero. We publish the result as it came out; the weights and pass marks were fixed before the run. In a second run, designed after seeing those totals, each analog was checked only on the challenges it is used for: 6 of 11 checks with enough sites pass, so the second run does not pass in full either. Pooled against ordinary places (pass mark 80%): Moon 84%, Mars 60%. A third run tried method version 1.1 (each part of a challenge counts equally, and the traits inside a part share its weight equally, plus a volcanic rock trait for Mars): 7 of 15 checks with enough sites pass, so version 1.1 does not pass in full either. On the held-out half, pooled against ordinary places: Moon 94% against 92% for version 1.0; Mars 66% against 64% for version 1.0. By the rule fixed before the run, version 1.1 is adopted and the map shows it.
not_blind_note: This is not a blind first run. A throwaway prototype scored the same test places twice on 14 November, and two lessons from it shaped this version. The weights and pass marks below were committed before this run, and the places marked blind had never been scored before.

third_run.method_change: The second run checked each known analog only on the challenges its papers say it is used for. Mars Surface failed clearly (21% against ordinary places, pass mark 80%). Jezero's crater floor is nearly flat, and so is farmland, while the slope traits carried most of the Surface weight and Mars had no rock trait at all, although Mars is a basalt world. Version 1.1 makes two changes that follow from Mars and from the team plan, not from the test places: it adds a volcanic rock trait for Mars (Mars's crust is basalt and Jezero's floor is igneous rock), and it replaces the hand-set trait weights with one rule for every challenge on both bodies: each part of a challenge, as the team plan lists them, counts equally, and the traits inside a part share its weight equally.
third_run.adoption_rule: Version 1.1 replaces version 1.0 on the site only if, on the held-out half, its pooled result against ordinary places (each analog on the challenges it is used for) is at least as high as version 1.0's for both the Moon and Mars. Otherwise version 1.0 stays and version 1.1 is reported as tried and not adopted.
